items.title: `cut-release.sh` bumps every crate's version but does not rebuild `crates/vilan-image-wasm/vilan_image.wasm`, so the release commit fails CI's wasm leg by construction: `build-image-wasm.sh --check` says the committed blob is NOT what the pinned toolchain builds from the tree (v0.54.0's release commit 7c11bea4; the parent 305f8721 was green)
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-03 (the integrator's find at the v0.54.0 cut)
items.discussion: M190 (Order 56) made the image blob REBUILT and byte-checked by CI; the version bump of vilan-image / vilan-image-wasm changes the build output (the crate version reaches the wasm), so every cut from now on lands a red wasm leg on the tag commit unless the blob is rebuilt in the release commit
items.body: Rec: cut-release.sh runs `scripts/build-image-wasm.sh` after the version bump and stages the blob in the release commit (and the §7.3 patch cut too); alternatively the byte check compares the blob with the version string masked. Pin: cut-release.sh's dry run reports `blob: rebuilt` / `blob: stale`. Sizing S. The v0.54.0 cut is the exhibit: owner question 11 says how it was resolved.

items.title: M176/M177's native peak-RSS pins (bound 8 MiB) read 24.9 MB (the 64 MiB stream) and 30.4 MB (the 10 MiB part) on CI's ubuntu gate shards at the v0.54.0 release commit, green on the same code one commit earlier - the native server's read-ahead grows under LOAD (two runs shared the self-hosted runner)
items.kind: harness (load-sensitive pins; M176) - possibly a native inbox bound
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-03 (the integrator's find at the v0.54.0 cut)
items.discussion: lane http-56 planted unbounded native read-ahead and read 29.7 MB - the same magnitude CI read under load; so either the bound is load-sensitive by nature (the client writes faster than a starved server reads and the kernel/inbox holds the difference) or the native inbox has no cap when the handler is slow, which is M176's own claim ('the cap counted as it reads') - decide which with a loaded repro (`stress -c 8` + the pin in a loop)
items.body: Rec: reproduce under load on the lane's harness; if the inbox grows past a piece, cap it (read at most one `size` ahead); if only the kernel's socket buffers grow, the pin bounds the WRONG number and should read the inbox's own high-water mark (an instrument like `refused_body_census`). Until then the two pins are flaky under a shared runner (N192 is the stream-race sibling). Sizing S-M.
